lines.text: Do you know how your phone finds you indoors, where GPS can't reach?
Deep inside a shopping mall, the satellite signals hit concrete. And yet the blue dot still knows where you are.
Your phone listens for every Wi-Fi network around. It doesn't join them. It just hears their names, and how loud they are.
Mapping cars, and millions of phones, have already noted where those routers sit.
Loud means close. Quiet means far. Draw a circle around each one, and where the circles cross, that's you!
No Wi-Fi? Cell towers do the same trick, only rougher.
Orbi Transfer goes the other way. Other people only ever see your rough area, a big patch of the map. Never your spot.
